current_parent_meaning_bindings.meaning: The Convention's dependence on Parisian popular power made the constitutional relation between the capital, elected national representatives, and the departments the chapter's central conflict. Sections and the democratized National Guard supplied coercive power, but Paris was internally divided: Muscadins briefly captured several sectional assemblies. Departmental-guard proposals sought protection for national deliberation; the same sectional forms served opposing provincial coalitions. Sectional pressure joined claims of popular guardianship to immediate subsistence demands, compelling the Convention to adopt grain and bread controls.

rows.lead_source_disposition: 232–233 connect sectional gains for property-defending opponents and absent Montagnards to threatened voting strength, then acceptance of the purge idea. Mere mention of Muscadins does not fully retain this causal explanation.
